speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Health in respect of the incident whereby blood donors' personal data are compromised (a) whether there are further updates from the preliminary investigation; (b) what follow-up actions have been carried out with the cybersecurity expert who discovered the vulnerability; (c) whether there is a framework in place to ensure that vendors comply with safeguards to prevent unsafe practices and unauthorised access to data; and (d) what measures are necessary to prevent future occurrences and to reassure future blood donors.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the exposure of blood donors' personal data online (a) whether the Ministry will consider streamlining the procurement of IT services across its departments, Statutory Boards, hospitals and clinics to reduce personal data access by multiple vendors; and (b) whether there are factors causing the public healthcare sector to be particularly vulnerable to IT incidents.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there has been any compensation or payment made to the cybersecurity expert who discovered and downloaded the unsecured HSA database containing the personal information of more than 800,000 blood donors; and (b) whether it is a condition set by the said expert that his identity should remain secret.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members of this House have asked for further updates on the preliminary investigation of the data leak of blood donors' personal information from the database of the vendor appointed by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Secur Solutions Group Ptd Ltd (Secur Solutions) is an independent vendor of HSA appointed to maintain and enhance the queue management system for blood donors.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: HSA immediately worked with Secur Solutions to disable access to the server.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 30 March, Secur Solutions issued a statement to provide more information on this incident.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Investigations are continuing and a further update will be provided when available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members have also asked questions relating to the cybersecurity expert.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The cybersecurity expert works for a company that specialises in identifying and reporting vulnerabilities of information technology (IT) systems.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He was not employed or engaged by HSA or the Ministry of Health (MOH).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members have asked what additional steps MOH and HSA can take to reduce the risk of data mismanagement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The measures to be taken to prevent a similar occurrence will be shaped by what specific findings arise from the ongoing investigations into the incident.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MOH and its agencies will also conduct a review on the lifecycle management of the data being handled by existing IT vendors.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, the HSA Board has set up a Board Committee chaired by Mr Max Loh, Chairman of HSA Board's Audit and Risk Committee.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Board Committee also includes members from Government Technology Agency (GovTech).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It will review HSA's current policies and processes for managing sensitive data and recommend measures.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MOH and its agencies will extend our fullest cooperation to the work of the Committee.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Iswaran, I believe you had asked to take the supplementary questions after responses to the next two Parliamentary Questions (PQs)?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I can take the supplementary questions now if Members —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe the request is to take them all together later.
